newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to revalue currency reserves in '97 - FDP.
newsitem.headline: Germany to revalue currency reserves in '97 - FDP.

text.p: The German government planned to revalue its foreign currency reserves in 1997, Hermann Otto Solms, parliamentary leader of the junior coalition partners Free Democrats (FDP), said on Tuesday.
Bonn would book profits from the transaction in 1998, he said.
The FDP, which has opposed tax increases to help Bonn close its budget deficit, was in favour of revaluations, if carried out under a joint plan between Bonn and the Bundesbank, Solms said.
"That would mean that the currency reserves are revalued in this year, and then the corresponding profits can follow next year," he said.
The Finance Ministry and the Bundesbank have agreed on a plan to revalue Germany's gold and currency reserves in steps beginning this year.
The transactions would would have no effect on the 19 billion mark budget shortfall expected in 1997 by Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
